# What Are the Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere?

Insights from IDC’s Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere research

The Global DataSphere measures how much new data the world generates each year, while the Global StorageSphere measures the installed base of storage capacity and how much of it is used. They answer different questions.

## What is the Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere?

The Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere are two IDC forecasts that size data from different angles. The Global DataSphere measures how much new data is generated in a year, and the Global StorageSphere measures the storage capacity installed to hold it. According to IDC, the DataSphere adds data created or captured to data replicated or consumed, while the StorageSphere is built from storage media shipments and retirement rates. This matters because only a small fraction of new data is ever stored, so the two numbers cannot be swapped.

According to IDC’s Worldwide Global DataSphere Taxonomy, 2026 (IDC #US54227826), the Global DataSphere is “not a measure of how much data is stored.” The Global StorageSphere is the companion measure of capacity. IDC research manager Adam Wright leads both programs, and IDC publishes each as its own forecast, taxonomy and set of vertical industry views.

## Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere Details

What it is. The Global DataSphere is a measure of how much new data is generated in any given year, counting data created or captured plus data replicated or consumed. The Global StorageSphere is a measure of the cumulative installed base of storage capacity across all storage media types, and how much of that base is utilized and available.

How it works. IDC builds the DataSphere from the installed base of data-creating devices, how those devices are used, file sizes and bit rates, and data replication needs such as backup and compliance. It builds the StorageSphere from historical and forecast storage media shipments and retirement rate assumptions. IDC reconciles the data saved in the StorageSphere with the DataSphere.

Why it matters. Mixing the two measures leads to wrong sizing. Data generation drives network, compute and AI infrastructure decisions, while installed storage capacity drives media, system and cost decisions. IDC’s DataSphere data type, location and vertical industry views give planners a defined baseline instead of a loose estimate.

## How does the Global DataSphere differ from the Global StorageSphere?

The DataSphere counts data generated in a year, and the StorageSphere counts storage capacity installed at the end of a year. IDC states that the DataSphere is not a cumulative number and not a measure of capacity. The StorageSphere is not a measure of how much data is created or replicated.

Supporting points

- DataSphere: new data created, captured, replicated or consumed in one year.
- StorageSphere: installed base of storage capacity, plus the share utilized and available, as a year-end snapshot.
- Only a small fraction of new data created each year is stored, so the DataSphere is far larger than annual data saved.

## What counts as data in the Global DataSphere?

The DataSphere is the sum of data created or captured and data replicated or consumed. IDC models the volume across 70 categories of data-creating devices. IDC also assigns replicated data to the device type it is copied to.

Supporting points

- Replicated and consumed data makes up roughly 90% of all data generated in IDC’s June 2026 forecast, driven by streaming, backup and multicloud copying.
- IDC treats generative AI and agentic AI as shifts in how data is generated and stored, and accounts for them in its models.
- Enterprise data generation is the foundation for IDC’s sector and vertical industry forecasts.

## What do ephemeral, cached and saved data mean?

IDC separates data by how long it lives. Ephemeral data lasts seconds, cached data is held temporarily on persistent storage, and saved data is kept beyond the year it was created. These definitions connect the DataSphere to the StorageSphere.

Supporting points

- Ephemeral data is created or replicated for consumption or analysis and typically has no path to persistent storage.
- Cached data is retained for less than one year and then deleted or overwritten.
- Saved data is stored on persistent storage beyond the current year, and IDC reconciles it with the Global DataSphere.

## What do IDC’s current forecasts show?

IDC’s June 2026 forecast puts worldwide data generation at 218,433 EB in 2025 and 718,484 EB in 2030, a 26.9% compound annual growth rate. IDC also expects the installed base of storage capacity to exceed 26 ZB in 2030.

Supporting points

- Enterprise data generation grows at a 31.1% CAGR against 13.5% for consumers, lifting the enterprise share of data from 70% in 2025 to 83% in 2030.
- Cloud data generation grows 38.9% annually, lifting its share from 27.0% to 43.0% by 2030.
- Edge data grows at a 31.9% CAGR, against 14.7% for endpoint devices.

## Supporting Evidence

> “The IDC Global DataSphere is on a trajectory to surpass 700ZB by 2030” — Adam Wright, Senior Research Manager, IDC Global DataSphere and IDC Global StorageSphere (IDC #US53425426, June 2026)

> “Storage economics are shifting as organizations balance performance, cost, resilience, and AI-enabled value.” — Adam Wright, Research Manager, IDC Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere (IDC #US54227926, January 2026)

## FAQ

### What is the Global DataSphere?

The Global DataSphere is IDC’s measure of how much new data is generated in a year, combining data created or captured with data replicated or consumed.

### What is the Global StorageSphere?

The Global StorageSphere is IDC’s measure of the installed base of storage capacity across all media types and how much of it is utilized and available.

### Is the Global DataSphere a measure of stored data?

No. IDC states that the DataSphere is not a measure of storage capacity or how much data is stored, and that only a small fraction of new data is stored.

### How much data will the world generate by 2030?

IDC’s June 2026 forecast puts annual data generation at 718,484 EB in 2030, up from 218,433 EB in 2025.

### Who produces IDC’s Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere forecasts?

They come from IDC’s Global DataSphere and Global StorageSphere research program, led by research manager Adam Wright.
